record.field:
Inelcom · Odoo Integration

1) Connection (Remote Control)

Type: REST · Base URL: https://smart.inelcom.com:6081/restws

connection_params (JSON):

{
  "username": "user_inelcom",
  "password": "********"
}
  • Login → performs POST /restws/webresources/sesiones and returns a plain session token string.
  • All subsequent requests must include the query parameter: 
    ?sesion=<token>
  • No logout endpoint is required.

2) Available Procedures

The following predefined procedures are included:

  • Inelcom: Daily Sync → automatically performs (1) device/sensor planning, (2) reading download, and (3) upsert of readings into Odoo.
  • Inelcom: Get Devices → fetches the complete list of available devices from Inelcom API for configuration purposes.

3) Typical Workflow

  1. Get Devices Plan:
    • Finds all sensors belonging to devices connected to this Inelcom remote control.
    • Reads remotecontrol_params from device and sensor records.
    • Extracts:
      • route (hydrant route)
      • device_id (counter identifier)
      • start_date if available
    • Determines initial_date based on:
      • last reading in Odoo, or
      • device start_date, or
      • sensor start_date, or
      • default: YYYY-01-01
    • Stores the resulting plan in bag["sensors_plan"].
  2. Get Readings Data:
    • Authenticates using POST /restws/webresources/sesiones.
    • For each sensor in the plan, computes the number of days to request.
    • Calls: 
      GET /isrlrestws/resources/hidrantes/<route>
    ?sesion=<token>
    &contador=<device_id>
    &fecha=<DD/MM/YY>
    &dias=<N>
    • Parses payload["lista"] and builds:
      • timestamp (date + hour)
      • numeric value
    • Generates a JSON audit attachment: 
      inelcom_readings_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json
    • Stores:
      • bag["raw_readings"]
      • bag["sensors_with_errors"]
      • bag["fetch_summary"]
      • bag["audit_attachment_id"]
  3. Upsert Readings:
    • Iterates through bag["raw_readings"].
    • Upserts into mdm.measurement.device.sensor.reading using: 
      Remote.upsert({
  key: { sensor_id, measurement_time },
  values: { value, device_id }
})
    • Updates counters: successful, failed.
    • Stores summary in bag["upsert_summary"].
    • Posts a message in the remote control chatter.

4) Device Discovery Workflow

  1. Get Devices List:
    • Authenticates using POST /restws/webresources/sesiones.
    • Fetches all sectors using: 
      GET /restws/webresources/nodos/sectores?sesion=<token>
    • For each sector, retrieves device counters: 
      GET /restws/webresources/hidrantes/contadores
    ?sesion=<token>
    §or=<sector_id>
    • Collects device information including:
      • counter_code (counter identifier)
      • name (hydrant name and counter number)
      • hydrant_id (hydrant ID)
      • value (current reading value)
      • sector (sector ID)
    • Generates a JSON attachment: 
      inelcom_devices_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json
    • Stores the complete device list in bag["inelcom_devices"].
    • This information can be used to configure remotecontrol_params for new devices.

5) Odoo Configuration

In Device (mdm.measurement.device):

{
  "device_id": "1234",       // counter identifier
  "start_date": "2025-01-01" // optional
}
  • device_id: Identifier used in Inelcom “contador”.
  • start_date: Default beginning date if the sensor has no readings.

In Sensor (mdm.measurement.device.sensor):

{
  "route": "45",             // hydrant route
  "start_date": "2025-01-01" // optional
}
  • route: Hydrant route/path in the Inelcom API.
  • start_date: Overrides device start_date.

Both route and device_id are required for synchronization.

6) Endpoints Used

  • POST /restws/webresources/sesiones → obtains plain session token.
  • GET /restws/webresources/nodos/sectores → retrieves list of available sectors.
  • GET /restws/webresources/hidrantes/contadores → retrieves device counters for a specific sector.
  • GET /isrlrestws/resources/hidrantes/<route> → retrieves readings (requires query parameters: sesion, contador, fecha, dias).

7) Generated File Structure

Reading Sync Files

The JSON audit attachment inelcom_readings_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json contains:

{
  "executed_at": "2025-10-14 09:37:24",
  "total_upserts": 120,
  "total_errors": 3,
  "items": [
    {
      "sensor_id": 12,
      "device_id": 107,
      "sensor_id_param": "45",
      "status": 200,
      "points_found": 56,
      "upserts": 56,
      "errors": 0,
      "readings_summary": [
        {"ts": "2025-10-13 12:00:00", "value": 3.2}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "sensors_in_plan": 32,
    "sensors_processed": 32,
    "success_rate": "93.8%"
  }
}

Device Discovery Files

The JSON attachment inelcom_devices_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.json contains:

{
  "executed_at": "2025-11-19 10:30:15",
  "total_devices": 245,
  "total_errors": 0,
  "devices": [
    {
      "counter_code": "12345",
      "name": "Hydrant A - Counter 001",
      "hydrant_id": "HYD001",
      "value": 1234.56,
      "sector": "SECTOR_01"
    }
  ],
  "errors": []
}

8) Recommendations

  • Use the Get Devices procedure to discover available devices before configuration.
  • Ensure each device and sensor has correct remotecontrol_params:
    • route
    • device_id
    • start_date (optional)
  • Check the generated attachment for diagnostics if errors appear.
  • If readings stop updating, verify:
    • the login endpoint is available,
    • the date range (initial_date) is correct,
    • the hydrant route and counter ID match Inelcom configuration.

import time Remote = self.remote_id
cfg = json.loads(Remote.connection_params or '{}') or {} username = (cfg.get('username') or '').strip() password = (cfg.get('password') or '').strip()
url = 'https://smart2.inelcom.com:28081/restws/webresources/sesiones' resp = request_retry('POST', url, json={'usuario': username, 'clave': password}, timeout=180) if resp.status_code >= 400: raise Exception("Login failed: %s %s" % (resp.status_code, resp.text)) id_session = resp.text.strip() if not id_session: raise Exception("Login OK but empty token")
sectors_url = "https://smart2.inelcom.com:28081/restws/webresources/nodos/sectores?sesion=%s" % id_session resp = request_retry('GET', sectors_url) if resp.status_code >= 400: raise Exception("Sector query failed: %s %s" % (resp.status_code, resp.text))
payload = resp.json() or {} sectors_list = payload.get("listaSectores", []) or [] devices = [] errors = []
for sector in sectors_list: sector_id = sector.get("idSector") if not sector_id: continue url = ( "https://smart2.inelcom.com:28081/restws/webresources/hidrantes/contadores" "?sesion=%s&sector=%s" ) % (id_session, sector_id) try: resp2 = request_retry('GET', url) if resp2.status_code >= 400: errors.append({'sector': sector_id, 'error': 'HTTP Error %d' % resp2.status_code}) continue data = resp2.json() or {} counters_list = data.get("listaContadores", []) for counter in counters_list: counter_code = counter.get("codContador") hydrant_name = counter.get("nombreHidrante") or "" counter_number = counter.get("numContador") or "" name = "%s - %s" % (hydrant_name, counter_number) devices.append({ 'counter_code': counter_code, 'name': name, 'hydrant_id': counter.get("idHidrante"), 'value': counter.get("valor"), 'sector': sector_id }) except Exception as e: errors.append({'sector': sector_id, 'error': str(e)}) time.sleep(0.5)
locations = [] locations_url = "https://smart2.inelcom.com:28081/restws/webresources/emplazamientos?sesion=%s" % id_session try: resp_locations = request_retry('GET', locations_url) if resp_locations.status_code >= 400: errors.append({'type': 'locations', 'error': 'HTTP Error %d' % resp_locations.status_code}) else: locations_list = resp_locations.json() or [] for location in locations_list: location_id = location.get("idEmplazamiento") location_name = location.get("nombreEmplazamiento") sector_name = location.get("nombreSector") header_name = location.get("nombreCabezal")
variables = [] if location_id: variables_url = ( "https://smart2.inelcom.com:28081/restws/webresources/emplazamientos/variables" "?sesion=%s&emplazamiento=%s" ) % (id_session, location_id) try: resp_vars = request_retry('GET', variables_url) if resp_vars.status_code >= 400: errors.append({ 'type': 'location_variables', 'location_id': location_id, 'error': 'HTTP Error %d' % resp_vars.status_code }) else: variables_list = resp_vars.json() or [] for var in variables_list: variables.append({ 'variable_id': var.get('id'), 'variable_name': var.get('nombre') }) except Exception as e: errors.append({ 'type': 'location_variables', 'location_id': location_id, 'error': str(e) }) time.sleep(0.5)
locations.append({ 'location_id': location_id, 'location_name': location_name, 'sector_name': sector_name, 'header_name': header_name, 'sector_code': location.get("codSector"), 'header_code': location.get("codCabezal"), 'variables': variables, 'total_variables': len(variables) }) time.sleep(0.5) except Exception as e: errors.append({'type': 'locations', 'error': str(e)})
result = { 'executed_at': fields.Datetime.now(), 'total_devices': len(devices), 'total_locations': len(locations), 'total_errors': len(errors), 'devices': devices, 'locations': locations, 'errors': errors, }
audit_json = json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=True, indent=2, default=str) b64 = base64.b64encode(audit_json) now_str = fields.Datetime.now().replace(':', '').replace('-', '') fname = 'inelcom_devices_%s.json' % now_str.replace(' ', '_') att = env['ir.attachment'].create({ 'name': fname, 'datas_fname': fname, 'datas': b64, 'mimetype': 'application/json', 'res_model': 'remotecontrol', 'res_id': Remote.id })
msg = "[Inelcom] Devices: %d, Locations: %d, Errors: %d" % (len(devices), len(locations), len(errors)) Remote.message_post(body=msg, attachment_ids=[att.id])
bag['inelcom_devices'] = devices bag['inelcom_locations'] = locations bag['inelcom_devices_errors'] = errors bag['inelcom_devices_filename'] = fname
